page: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.metal is a bare-metal instance within the memory-optimized family, designed for high-density transactional and analytical workloads. It operates directly on physical hardware without a hypervisor layer, providing access to 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs driven by Intel Xeon 8375C processors on the x86_64 architecture. The system reaches clock speeds up to 3.5 GHz and incorporates 54 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction sets such as AVX-512, VNNI, VAES, and SHA-NI. Memory capacity is substantial at 4096 GB of DDR4 RAM clocked at 3 GHz, yielding an allocation of 32 GB per physical core. Storage and networking subsystems include 3800 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, with zero integrated GPUs.

In synthetic and practical benchmarks, the bare-metal architecture exhibits top-tier multi-threaded processing and memory throughput. Multi-core stress-ng tests reach 124,967.29, while PassMark CPU encryption and extended instruction tests score in the top ten percent. Measured memory bandwidth registers 311.12 GB/sec for large uncached reads and 120.27 GB/sec for large writes. In operational database benchmarks, x2iedn.metal completed 109.38 million Redis SET operations per second and registered strong scores in PassMark database execution. While prompt processing benchmarks for small to medium language models maintain strong throughput, text generation on 70B parameter models remains weak at 2.63 tokens per second, illustrating the CPU-bound limits of transformer decoding without dedicated accelerators.

From an efficiency perspective, x2iedn.metal enables extreme resource consolidation by packaging 4 TB of volatile memory with fast local NVMe storage and high network capacity into a single dedicated node. The primary tradeoff lies in per-thread execution speed, where single-core stress-ng and Geekbench metrics remain in the middle tier despite the massive parallel capacity. The configuration is best matched to in-memory databases such as SAP HANA or Redis, large-scale electronic design automation, distributed memory cache layers, and real-time big data analytics pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services x2iedn.metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized instance engineered for large-scale enterprise workloads requiring substantial memory density and direct hardware access. Powered by dual Intel Xeon 8375C processors running on the x86_64 architecture, the platform features 64 physical cores, 128 vCPUs at up to 3.5 GHz, and an expansive 4096 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz. Local storage includes 3800 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, complemented by a 100 Gbps baseline network interface. Benchmark results reflect top-tier multithreaded CPU performance, strong cryptographic throughput via AVX-512 and AES acceleration, and substantial memory read speeds exceeding 311 GB/sec. Without virtualization overhead, the instance sustains over 109 million Redis operations per second. However, single-thread performance remains average, and LLM text generation scaling degrades on large models due to lack of GPU acceleration. This profile makes x2iedn.metal well suited for large in-memory databases, electronic design automation, big data analytics engines, and cache clusters.
